interest: Shows 1940-41 U.S. alarm over Japanese census-taking of Spanish speakers and diaspora loyalty, feeding pre-Pearl Harbor intelligence.
overview: Docket for file 894.5011 (Dec 1940-Dec 1941) covers Japanese census and registration of nationals, including Justice Department queries on the Fourth Census, alarm over a census of Spanish-speaking Japanese prompting Latin American diplomatic alerts, Kilsoo Haan's reports on illegal immigration, Shanghai foreign-resident censuses, and Hawaii Nisei census surveillance.

subfiles.about: The Department of Justice transmits a Japanese Fourth Census questionnaire and inquires whether it is being distributed to non-national Japanese Americans.
subfiles.summary: Justice Department sends a translated Japanese Fourth Census questionnaire and asks State whether it was distributed to American citizens of Japanese ancestry lacking Japanese nationality.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of Justice on Japanese Fourth Census Questionnaire

subfiles.about: The War Department forwards an official communication concerning the Japanese government's registration of its nationals.
subfiles.summary: War Department forwards a communication on Japan's registration of nationals, routed to State's Far Eastern Division and related offices.
subfiles.title: Communication from War Department on Registration of Japanese Nationals

subfiles.about: The Department of Justice reports that the Japanese census applies strictly to Japanese nationals and dual citizens, not non-national Japanese Americans.
subfiles.summary: Justice Department confirms Japan's Fourth Census was restricted to Japanese nationals and dual citizens, with no questionnaires distributed to Americans of Japanese race lacking Japanese nationality.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of Justice on Japanese Census and Dual Citizens

subfiles.about: U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits published population statistics for the Japanese Empire from the 1940 census.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 5547: Grew forwards official 1940 census statistics for the Japanese Empire, published in the government's Official Gazette on April 18, 1941.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5547 from Grew on 1940 Population Census of the Japanese Empire

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports a Japanese census of Spanish-speaking nationals, prompting a State Department circular to Latin American missions.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 1144: Grew reports Japan is censusing Spanish-speaking nationals; State's August 6, 1941 circular instructs envoys across the American Republics to alert host foreign ministers.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1144 from Grew on Japanese Census of Spanish Speakers and State Department Circular

subfiles.about: Ambassador Daniels reports that Mexico's Foreign Minister was alerted to the Japanese census of Spanish speakers and pledged hemispheric protection.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 378: Ambassador Daniels reports Mexico's Foreign Minister, informed of Japan's Spanish-speaker census, assured that Japanese residents would do nothing in Mexico against Western Hemisphere interests.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 378 from Daniels on Japanese Census of Spanish Speakers and Mexican Assurances

subfiles.about: Minister Boal reports transmitting State Department instructions on the Japanese census of Spanish speakers to the Nicaraguan Foreign Minister.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 16: Minister Boal confirms Nicaragua's Foreign Minister was notified of Japan's census of Spanish-speaking nationals, per State's instructions.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 16 from Boal on Japanese Census of Spanish Speakers in Nicaragua

subfiles.about: Kilsoo Haan of the Sino-Korean Peoples' League reports on illegal Japanese entrants in the Western Hemisphere and Hawaii, urging review of consular records.
subfiles.summary: Kilsoo Haan of the Sino-Korean Peoples' League reports illegal Japanese immigration into the Western Hemisphere, including Hawaii, and urges requiring Japanese consulates to disclose past census and registration records.
subfiles.title: Letter from Sino-Korean Peoples' League (Haan) on Illegal Japanese Entrants in the Western Hemisphere

subfiles.about: The U.S. Consul-General at Shanghai reports on census-taking of foreign residents in the Western Shanghai area.
subfiles.summary: The Shanghai Consul-General reports on a census of foreign residents in Western Shanghai, forwarding a circular letter seeking cooperation from the Danish Consul-General and the Senior Consul.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Consul-General at Shanghai on Census of Foreign Residents in Western Shanghai

subfiles.about: The War Department transmits a Hawaiian Intelligence Division report regarding censuses of native and American-born Japanese.
subfiles.summary: War Department forwards a Hawaiian Intelligence Division report noting censuses underway of both native Japanese and American-born Japanese (Nisei) in Hawaii, weeks before Pearl Harbor.
subfiles.title: Report from War Department on Census of Native and American-Born Japanese in Hawaii
